articles.title: Continued Use of Houge Park Uncertain
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) faces an uncertain future regarding its use of Houge Park, as the City of San Jose is soliciting proposals for "reuse" of older community centers. The SJAA must submit a compelling proposal and secure legal counsel by August 22, 2008, to transition to a formal contractual agreement, otherwise, the club will lose its primary venue for meetings and star parties. This crucial process will determine the club's long-term operations and existence as currently known.

articles.title: Join the Summer Twilight Dance
articles.summary: This article highlights celestial events for August, focusing on a prominent 'dance' between Saturn, Venus, and Mercury in the evening twilight sky, with Mars joining in early September, offering the best evening views of Mercury all year. While total solar and partial lunar eclipses are not visible from North America, observers can enjoy bright views of Jupiter, and seek out Neptune (at opposition), Uranus, and Pluto throughout the month.

articles.title: Star-B-Q 2008
articles.summary: The Star-B-Q 2008 event, held on August 2nd at Fremont Peak State Park, invited astronomy enthusiasts to a potluck picnic, annual meeting, and super star party. It featured a keynote address by Dr. Peter Jenniskens on "Meteor Showers and their Parent Comets," an astronomical-themed dish contest, and opportunities to observe the night sky with the 30-inch Challenger Telescope. Attendees were encouraged to RSVP and bring a dish to share for this social and educational astronomy gathering.

articles.title: Space Buoys
articles.summary: The article highlights the challenge of studying Earth's vast magnetosphere with single spacecraft, likening it to understanding an entire ocean with just one buoy. It introduces NASA's Space Technology 5 (ST5) mission, which in 2006 launched three experimental micro-satellites that successfully demonstrated the feasibility and benefits of using a constellation of small spacecraft with miniaturized technology to comprehensively map complex space environments. This mission validated crucial technologies and proved that multiple spacecraft working together are essential for future magnetosphere studies.

articles.title: The Last 31 Days In Astronomy
articles.summary: The article provides a digest of astronomy news from July 2008, detailing events such as Jupiter's Little Red Spot disappearing, a spacewalk on the International Space Station, the impending retirement of the Space Shuttle, and new discoveries from STEREO, SOHO, and Cassini missions. Additionally, it features an obituary for Paul Barton, a passionate amateur astronomer, telescope maker, and long-time member of the SJAA, who passed away on July 4th.

articles.title: Yosemite Star Party Report
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) held its annual public star party at Glacier Point in Yosemite on the July 4th weekend in 2008. Despite some haze from wildfires and minor clouds, participants enjoyed two nights of dark skies and good views, especially through a 22" Dobsonian, though public attendance was lower than usual. The report also lists attendees and highlights the scenic location.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) operates a Telescope Loaner Program, enabling members to try a diverse range of astronomical equipment, including various telescopes and binoculars, before purchasing. This program, a significant member benefit, temporarily ceased operations until August 7th at the time of writing, with an inventory list provided. The document also outlines the club's officers, contact information, and details regarding their monthly newsletter, the SJAA Ephemeris.
